answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ—a direct signal. Both memory_86 (shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup simplification improved SMB activation) point to the same lever and showed durable lift. Activation messaging (memory_91) and referral incentives (memory_57) address engagement downstream, not the upstream friction. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitive pressure, but it risks margin and trains price-sensitive cohorts into discount dependency. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is high-value but slower to measure and doesn't address the 6% activation drop or 4% completion decline. Simplifying onboarding directly targets the observed metric deterioration, likely recovers near-term activation, and compounds into better long-term quality revenue. Verification of these two memories will confirm whether the prior lift was durable across changing conditions and whether field reduction/flow simplification remains effective in current SMB behavior.
